consigna.es: Escucha y elige qué dice la hablante sobre su hermana.

items.audio: My sister will interrupt me every time I start a story. Yesterday she did it again, just when I reached the best part. It is so annoying.
opciones: Her sister is going to interrupt her tomorrow.
Her sister often does this, and she hates it.
Her sister did this only once, yesterday.

feedback.es: «Will» describe una costumbre típica (no un futuro); con «every time» y «so annoying» se ve que lo hace a menudo y le molesta.

consigna.es: Escucha y elige qué pasó con la prisa.

items.audio: We needn't have hurried. When we arrived, the hall was half empty, because the concert wasn't due to start for another hour. Next time, we'll leave later and have dinner first.
opciones: They arrived after the concert had started.
They took their time because they knew it was early.
They rushed, but there was no need to.

feedback.es: «Needn't have hurried» significa que corrieron y resultó innecesario: llegaron con una hora de sobra. No es lo mismo que no correr.

consigna.es: Escucha y elige qué se concluye sobre la leyenda del puente.

items.audio: It is said that the old bridge is haunted. The mayor denied that anything strange has ever happened there, and the historian admitted that nobody has any proof, although the legend is very old.
opciones: Both officials say the bridge is really haunted.
The legend is old, but there is no evidence for it.
The historian found proof, but the mayor denied it.

feedback.es: Se dice que está encantado, pero el alcalde lo niega y el historiador admite que nadie tiene pruebas: la leyenda es antigua y sin evidencia.

consigna.es: Escucha y elige qué opina la persona sobre los móviles y el sueño.

items.audio: Some teachers argue that phones help students learn, given that they can look up information quickly. However, the survey suggests that the more students use their phones at night, the less they sleep. That does not prove phones are the only cause.
opciones: Phones may harm sleep, but other causes are possible.
Phones are the only cause of students' sleep problems.
Phones do not affect sleep, because they help students learn.

feedback.es: Reconoce una posible relación con el sueño, pero aclara que no prueba que los móviles sean la única causa.

consigna.es: Lee la anécdota y elige por qué la autora dice «So there I am».

items.texto: Last Friday I was at the station when I noticed that my ticket was missing. So there I am, on the platform, checking every pocket, and the train is arriving. I sprint to the machine, grab a ticket and run back just as the whistle blows. The doors close behind me. Honestly, those thirty seconds felt like an hour, and my heart is still racing!
opciones: To say that she is still waiting at the station today
To make the scene feel as if it were happening now
To show that she often loses her ticket

feedback.es: El presente histórico («So there I am») acerca la escena al lector y la hace más vívida.

consigna.es: Lee la noticia y elige qué se sabe con seguridad.

items.texto: The mayor is said to have resigned last night, although the council has not confirmed the news. After reading the report on the old bridge, two neighbours claim that the repairs should have started years ago. The mayor's office denied that there was any danger. No sooner had the news arrived than shoppers began to ask whether the bridge would stay open. Nobody has said anything official yet.
opciones: The council has announced that the mayor resigned.
The mayor's office has accepted that the bridge is dangerous.
The news that the mayor resigned is not confirmed.

feedback.es: «Is said to have resigned» y «has not confirmed» indican un rumor sin confirmar; la oficina del alcalde, además, negó el peligro.

consigna.es: Lee el mensaje y elige cuál es el propósito principal de Mia.

items.texto: Hi Leo, I see your point about the cost, but I'm afraid the schedule is too tight. The party is due to start at six on Saturday, and the food is set to arrive at four. I will pay half on condition that you book the room. Could we postpone the party to 27 June instead? I'd appreciate it if you could let me know today. Thanks, Mia
opciones: To offer a compromise and suggest a new date
To reject Leo's idea and end the discussion
To ask Leo to pay everything to keep the party on Saturday

feedback.es: Mia reconoce el argumento de Leo, ofrece pagar la mitad con una condición y propone otra fecha: busca un punto medio.

consigna.es: Lee el texto y elige cuál es la postura de la autora.

items.texto: Critics argue that closing the city centre to cars would hurt local shops. The evidence, however, points the other way: in towns that tried it, the number of shoppers rose by a third, given that more people walked. What worries traders is not the ban itself but the change. A few months later, most of them would not go back to the old way, and the sales figures keep rising.
opciones: She agrees that shops will lose many customers.
She thinks the ban is more likely to help shops than harm them.
She believes traders will never accept the ban.

feedback.es: Presenta la objeción («Critics argue») y la rebate con datos («points the other way»): los comercios ganan clientes.

consigna.es: Completa la frase sobre el abuelo con la forma correcta.

items.texto: My grandfather is ninety, but every afternoon he ___ sit in the garden for hours, humming old songs.
opciones: will
would
used to

feedback.es: «Will» expresa una conducta típica en el presente; «would» y «used to» hablan de hábitos del pasado.

consigna.es: Elige la forma que completa la frase enfática.

items.texto: Hardly ___ the band started when the power went out.
opciones: did
had
was

feedback.es: Tras «hardly» se invierte el auxiliar y se usa el pasado perfecto: «Hardly had… when…».

consigna.es: Elige la forma que une las dos acciones, hechas por los mismos estudiantes.

items.texto: ___ the exam, the students left the room quietly.
opciones: Having been finished
Having finished
To have finished

feedback.es: «Having + participio» presenta una acción terminada antes de la principal, con el mismo sujeto: primero acabaron, luego salieron.

consigna.es: Elige la palabra que completa la frase enfática.

items.texto: ___ was the noise, not the price, that worried her.
opciones: What
It
Which

feedback.es: La frase enfática «It was… that…» destaca un elemento: aquí, el ruido y no el precio.

consigna.es: Elige la palabra que mejor completa la frase.

items.texto: It was such a ___ memory that I could still smell the smoke.
opciones: vague
vivid
weak

feedback.es: «Vivid» es muy claro y detallado; «vague» y «weak» indican un recuerdo borroso, lo contrario de lo que dice la frase.

consigna.es: Elige el verbo que encaja con el contexto.

items.texto: The report does not prove it, but two workers ___ that the company hid the results.
opciones: deny
allege
regret

feedback.es: «Allege» es afirmar algo sin pruebas; «deny» y «regret» no encajan con «does not prove it, but».

consigna.es: Elige el adjetivo que mejor describe a la líder.

items.texto: A good leader is ___: she stays calm when a plan fails.
opciones: level-headed
open-minded
impatient

feedback.es: «Level-headed» es mantener la calma y pensar con claridad; «open-minded» es aceptar ideas ajenas.

consigna.es: Elige la expresión que completa la frase.

items.texto: Constant rewards can ___ a change in our habits.
opciones: bring up
bring back
bring about

feedback.es: «Bring about» significa provocar o causar un cambio; «bring up» es mencionar o criar y «bring back» es devolver.

consigna.es: Dile con tacto a un amigo que debió avisarte: ya compraste la cena. Propón otro día.

items.respuesta: I was wondering if we could talk about dinner. You should have told me earlier, because I had already bought the food. Could we have dinner on Saturday instead?
aceptadas: I'm sorry to say this, but you should have called me earlier because I had already bought the food. Would it be possible to meet on Saturday instead?

feedback.es: Se espera «should have + participio» para el reproche, el motivo, una propuesta cortés y algún matiz de tacto.

consigna.es: Cuenta un rumor sobre el cierre de un parque y da tu opinión con un motivo (2–3 frases).

items.respuesta: It is said that the council is going to close the park next year. Given that many families use it every day, I think this would be a mistake.
aceptadas: The council is said to be closing the park soon. Given that families use it every day, closing it would be a bad idea.

feedback.es: Se espera una estructura impersonal para el rumor, tu opinión y un motivo («given that», «because»…).

notes: Escucha 1-4: opciones reparafraseadas sin eco del audio; escucha 2 ahora distingue needn't have de didn't need to.
Vocabulario 2 (denied) y gramática 4 (may well) eran de N5: sustituidos por allege y cleft It was...that (N6).
Gramática 3 cambiada a cláusula de participio (Having finished) para no filtrar is said to have de lectura 2/escucha 3; lectura 2 sin Having read.
Escritura 1: la consigna incluye ya el dato de la cena; rúbrica con grupo de tacto. Escritura 2: rúbrica ampliada (rumor impersonal, opinión, motivo).
Consignas de vocabulario sin glosa de la clave; distractores más plausibles en lectura 2-4.
